tasks.task: Write a commercial proposal for one deal

items.when: When you have call notes, the buyer's brief and the price list and need the full proposal
When you start from a sales call and want the follow-up, costing, margin check and dates in order
When the buyer should choose between good, better and best options instead of one price
When the buyer will line your offer up against cheaper ones, to see if it reads as the same thing
Before sending, to have a fresh reader go through it as the buyer and list what they would ask
When the proposal tells your story first and the buyer's question is answered on page four

tasks.task: Draft answers to tender and RFP questions

items.when: When the questions are listed and you must answer each from the client's own facts
Before drafting, to sort requirements into must-have and scored and see where proof is thin
When you want a second outline that shows which win theme each section should carry
When an answer is over the word limit and must lose words without losing a scored point
Before sign-off, so every number, certificate and client name in an answer has a dated source
When answers are padded and the marker has to dig for the point that earns the score

tasks.task: Decide whether to bid, with a scored bid or no-bid sheet

items.when: When a tender pack arrives and the client must decide if it is worth the writing time
When you want a second fit score and win-chance estimate from the buyer's own requirements
When the client faces many small bids a week and needs fast go or no-go calls on each
When the team already wants to bid, to hear the three best reasons not to

tasks.task: Build a requirements and compliance matrix from the pack

items.when: When you must list every instruction and requirement with where it is answered and by whom
When the matrix is the first step of a full bid and you need the later steps lined up
When the requirements need owners and sign-off tracked through to the final check
When the pack runs to hundreds of pages and you need each document cut to what matters first

tasks.task: Agree win themes and the proof for each

items.when: After the bid decision and before writing, to fix two to five reasons the buyer should pick you
When the client cannot say why they win, to find it in notes on past won and lost deals
When you know the incumbent or main rival and the themes must beat that one firm
When you have testimonials and case studies and must pick which backs each theme and where
When the themes are drafted, to test them against the toughest doubts an evaluator would raise
When a theme is a boast with no proof a sceptical buyer would believe

tasks.task: Write the executive summary a decision maker reads first

items.when: When the answers are drafted and you need the one or two pages that carry the whole case
When you want a second five-part summary draft to compare with your own
When the source is a long technical answer set and you need the answer and the numbers up front
When the summary tries to say everything, to name the one idea and cut what fights it
When you have two or three summary drafts and want a fresh reader to pick one
When the summary needs the answer first and the reasons grouped under it

tasks.task: Answer a security or vendor questionnaire

items.when: When a buyer sends a questionnaire and each answer must come from the client's real controls
When you need a sourced draft, an evidence index and a list of questions the team must answer
Before claiming a standard is met, to see the gaps against SOC 2 or ISO 27001
Before sending, so every yes in the form points to a policy or record with a date

tasks.task: Plan a grant bid: funder fit, outcomes, measures and budget

items.when: When a funder's call is open and you must plan the application against its own criteria
When the client has a programme but no funder yet, to shortlist funders with fit and dates
When the funder asks how activities lead to change and nothing is mapped
When the form asks how results will be measured and reported, and by whom
When the budget page needs programme costs and shared costs split in a way a funder accepts

tasks.task: Draft a grant application or letter of inquiry

items.when: When the plan is agreed and each section must be written to the funder's headings and limits
When you want a second draft built straight from the funder rules, programme facts and budget
When the funder wants a short letter of inquiry first, with a list of claims to prove
When it is a research grant, to critique aims and check the agency's rules
When a section is over the character limit in the funder's portal
Before submission, to have a fresh reader score the draft as the funder's assessor would

tasks.task: Write short replies to freelance job posts

items.when: When you paste a job post from a marketplace and need a short reply that shows fit fast
When you want a different shape to try: a numbered offer that ends in a proof you will run
When the replies read like a template and the client skims past them
When a bid runs long and the client will only read the first three lines
Before sending, to see which lines in the reply the freelancer cannot back with past work

tasks.task: Write a freelance profile, portfolio blurbs and gig listings

items.when: When a marketplace profile is new or undersells the freelancer and needs a headline and overview
When the profile headline is flat, to compare several honest angles
When past projects are only notes and each needs a short write-up of role, work and result
When the freelancer has no reviews yet and must ask past clients for a few lines
When the profile is drafted, to read it as a client who has ten other profiles open

tasks.task: Design service packages and the price section

items.when: When a freelancer needs three service packages with clear limits for a gig listing
When you need good, better and best tiers with a reason for each price point
When the offer needs value framing, payment terms and a name, not only a number
When a small first job should lead to bigger work and you need the steps planned
When the buyer fears the risk and a guarantee the client can afford would settle it
When the packages differ only by hours and none makes the result feel more certain

tasks.task: Price and quote a freelance project

items.when: When a project brief arrives and you need scope, price assumptions and contract risks in one quote
Before quoting, to turn target pay, costs and billable hours into an hourly and day rate
When you need a fee, billing terms and a limit on how much one client can take up
When past invoices exist, to see each client's real rate before you quote the next job

tasks.task: Write the scope, exclusions and statement of work

items.when: When the proposal needs what is in, what is out and what the buyer must supply, in plain words
When the buyer wants a separate statement of work with the usual clauses for the country
When the buyer asks for extras after the proposal, to compare the request with the agreed scope
Before sending terms, to rate the clauses that could cost the client later

tasks.task: Summarise tender terms or a contract in plain words

items.when: When the client needs a two-minute read of the contract terms before deciding to bid
When the buyer's terms look one-sided, to flag risky clauses and when to call a lawyer
When the client may ask for changes and needs clause edits plus a summary for their lawyer

tasks.task: Write the delivery plan, timeline and risk section

items.when: When the buyer scores a method or delivery answer and it must match what the client can do
When there are two real ways to deliver, to put both on a page with money and dates and pick one
When the answer needs a plan with owners, dependencies and a risk list across several teams
When the buyer asks for a risk register with scores and what you will do about each risk

tasks.task: Plan the bid: calendar, owners and review points

items.when: When a bid is a go and every step from questions deadline to upload needs a date and an owner
When several people supply answers and you need a weekly status and a chase list

tasks.task: Check a draft proposal against the buyer's brief

items.when: When the draft is done, to tick every requirement in the matrix against where it is answered
When you want a fresh reader to go through the draft as the buyer with only the brief in hand
When the draft makes claims, to see which are backed, which go too far and how to fix them
When the draft reads well to you, to find the objections it has not answered
When the draft is full of in-house terms the buyer's panel will not know

tasks.task: Build and maintain a reusable answer bank

items.when: Monthly, to add new answers, retire old ones and note which results each answer has earned
When starting from nothing, to pull the client's services, customers and approved claims with sources
When stored answers quote dated numbers or certificates that may have run out
When the bank needs short case studies written from project notes and results
When a customer has agreed to talk and you need a case outline and what they must approve

tasks.task: Find and screen tenders and grants worth chasing

items.when: Weekly, to scan the client's notice sources and screen what is new against the bid sheet
When you need a shortlist of open grants and bids with a go or no-go reason for each
When the client is a nonprofit and needs funders matched to one programme and place
When you must look up a buyer or funder and want answers with source links to check

tasks.task: Write a shortlist presentation or demo script

items.when: When the buyer invites you to present and you need an outline that ends in a clear decision
When you need the deck outline, a one-pager or a demo script for this one buyer
When the panel should see two shapes of the offer side by side, with money and dates
When the panel will ask hard questions and the presenters need an answer with proof for each
When the deck is drafted, to check slide count, talk time and type size against the slot

tasks.task: Follow up a sent proposal and prepare the price talk

items.when: When a proposal has gone quiet and each follow-up needs a new reason and a stop rule
Before chasing, to work out if the buyer doubts you, is still comparing or fears a mistake
When the buyer asks for a lower price and the client needs an opening, questions and a fallback
When the buyer pushes on price and the client is about to give way without asking anything back

tasks.task: Debrief a win or loss and update the bid sheet

items.when: After a result, to turn the buyer's scores and feedback into fixes for answers and the bid sheet
When several bids were lost in a month and you want the real reasons across them

always.when: Before any bid leaves, so each fact has a dated source, a rewrite or is cut
Before upload, to catch typos and a buyer or product name spelt two ways
When any section reads like a brochure and needs plain words a marker can score

helpers.when: When the price model, discounts or tiers need real work before they go in a bid
When the buyer wants a demo, a pilot plan or deep technical and security answers
When the grant is part of a wider funding plan with funder research and reporting
When a security questionnaire shows real control gaps that must be fixed, not worded
When the proposal or shortlist deck must be laid out to a design standard
When a long bid from many authors needs one voice and a final proofread

gaps: No library item covers public tender rules by country: UK Procurement Act notices, US federal solicitations or EU forms
No library item scores a draft answer against the buyer's published marking scheme and weights
No library item writes social value, sustainability or equality answers for a tender
No library item writes freelance marketplace profiles, gig listings or bid replies; only the kit prompts cover them
No library item stores, versions and retires past answers as an answer bank
No library item builds a bid calendar with owners and review rounds; a general project agent stands in
No library item writes team CVs and bios to a bid's format
No library item prices a tender: a price schedule, day rates and the margin at each discount
No library item checks a submission against portal rules: file names, formats, page limits and signatures
No library item makes two or three clearly different proposal structures or cover pages to compare
No library item watches tender and grant notice sites for a client's keywords
